# `vendor/` — vendor Windows tooling (reference only, **not committed**)

This directory held the vendor's Windows configuration app, `MINI_KEYBOARD.exe`, used as
reverse-engineering evidence for the protocol this repo's CLI implements. The binaries
are **not tracked in git** (see `.gitignore`: only this README is tracked) — the archive
is still published by the vendor, so re-download it instead of vendoring 102 MB.

Nothing here is needed to build or run `ch57x-keyboard-tool`. The findings derived from
it live in
[`doc/documentation.md` → Vendor tool reverse engineering](../doc/documentation.md#vendor-tool-reverse-engineering).

## How to obtain it

```bash
cd vendor
curl -L -O "https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0655/8570/9299/files/New_English_software_is_set_in_the_upgrade_model-20250318.7z"
mv New_English_software_is_set_in_the_upgrade_model-20250318.7z new_software.7z
7z x new_software.7z            # -> "New English software is set in the upgrade model-20250318/"
```

| Check | Value |
|---|---|
| SHA-256 of the archive | `701a30fec3400437bd8c7f9005e35b9b4f2d0a3e6a27088fef0b50b7c30ecf03` |
| Size | 20,753,964 bytes (solid LZMA2, block 1) |
| Extracted size | 85,865,119 bytes — 71 files, 4 folders |
| Archive timestamp | 2025-03-18 |

The download URL was verified against the copy analysed here on **2026-09-17** — the
downloaded file hashed identically, so the reference copy is fully reproducible.

Source page (SIKAI CASE support, files on their Shopify CDN):
<https://sikaicase.com/blogs/support/setting-for-software>. Related downloads on the same
CDN, in case that build disappears or you need a different revision:
`release.7z`, `Update-20230714.zip`, `LEN-mac_OS.zip` (macOS tool). Expect **no license
grant** — the archive ships no license text; treat it as proprietary, for
interoperability study only.

## What the archive contains

It is not a clean app bundle: it is the vendor's leftover **MinGW build directory**,
shipped by accident, which is exactly why it is useful.

Extracted folder: `New English software is set in the upgrade model-20250318/`
(the vendor's own "English" name for the release).

| Group | Files | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| The app | `MINI_KEYBOARD.exe` (2.4 MB) | 32-bit Qt GUI; needs Windows (or Wine) + the bundled `hidapi.dll` |
| **Unstripped objects** | 23 × `.o` | `widget.o` (protocol core), `main.o`, `dialog1/2/3.o`, `form1.o`, `tabwidget.o`, `reminderwidget.o`, `thread.o`, `qrc_image.o`, `moc_*.o`, `ANTICATER_*_resource_res.o`, `lanague_resource_res.o` |
| Generated sources | 10 × `.cpp` + `moc_predefs.h` | `moc_widget.cpp`, `moc_dialog1/2/3.cpp`, `moc_form0/1/one.cpp`, `moc_reminderwidget.cpp`, `moc_thread.cpp` (Qt meta-object code → class/slot names); `qrc_image.cpp` is 8 MB of embedded PNG byte arrays |
| Build system | `Makefile`, `Makefile.Debug`, `Makefile.Release`, `object_script.KEY_PRO.{Debug,Release}` | header reads *"Generated by qmake (3.1) (Qt 5.14.2)"*, `CXX = g++`, paths `mingw73_32` / `mingw730_32` → Qt 5.14.2 + MinGW GCC 7.3, 32-bit, project `KEY_PRO.pro` |
| Qt / runtime DLLs | 13 top-level + `platforms/` (9.2 MB), `imageformats/` (2.1 MB), `styles/` (0.3 MB) | `Qt5Core/Gui/Widgets/Svg.dll`, `hidapi.dll`, `libgcc_s_dw2-1`, `libstdc++-6`, `libwinpthread-1`, `opengl32sw.dll` (16 MB), `libGLESv2`, `libEGL`, `D3Dcompiler_47.dll`, `msvcr100d.dll`, `qwindows.dll`, image-format plugins |
| Translations | `lanague_en.qm`, `lanague_enold.qm`, `lanague_cn.qm` | compiled Qt locales (note the vendor's misspelling of "language") |

### Key artifacts (checksums for the copy used in the notes)

| File | Size | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `MINI_KEYBOARD.exe` | 2,406,912 B | `334ae8358fbb3e3d5d76c05378cd7407f365bc390ab5377fc88a364a0f717b6e` |
| `widget.o` | 1,001,199 B | `06c3c3a0b9fa1336fb765eeafae7fe105830703148a3a776922207556ddb8898` |

`file` on the exe: `PE32 executable (GUI) Intel 80386 (stripped to external PDB), 9 sections`.
`widget.o` still carries ~200 defined symbols — enough to name the protocol functions.

## Re-running the analysis

```bash
nm --defined-only "New English software is set in the upgrade model-20250318/widget.o" | grep " T "
strings MINI_KEYBOARD.exe | grep -i "led_mode\|keyboard"      # e.g. LED_Mode_2, "Please select your keyboard"
```

For deeper work, import `widget.o` into Ghidra (ELF 32-bit LE, MinGW) — the symbol names
survive, so no blind disassembly is needed. Look for `Identify_KeyBoard_style()`, the
`Set_Keyboard_<N>add<M>` layout initialisers, and the hidapi calls
(`hid_enumerate` / `hid_open` / `hid_write` / `hid_read_timeout`).
